## Source: amazon-inspector (80ebf92f2c8c6fbaa83d432bf19aaa582ba6b4a0d775ff614fe7faa1cfcd987c)
The package ships only a package.json with description 'test', an empty dependencies list, a declared main (index.js) that is not present in the tarball, and config.unsafe-perm set to true. Its preinstall lifecycle script runs a node one-liner that hex-encodes process.cwd(), splits the hex into DNS-label-sized chunks, and issues a dns.lookup against <hex-chunks>.google.com. On npm install, this emits the installer's current working directory path (which typically reveals the OS username, host layout, and project name) as a DNS query, where passive DNS collectors and the authoritative resolver on the attacker-controlled suffix can harvest it. The google.com suffix is used as cover; the exfiltrated content is encoded into the subdomain labels. The package provides no advertised functionality — the entire shipped payload is the install-time beacon, consistent with a dependency-confusion / reconnaissance probe.
